ACTION AGENDA
The Action Agenda of the City Council Meeting is a document provided immediately following the Council Meeting in order for staff and the public to be aware of the business transacted and actions taken by Council. This is a preliminary draft and not a public record. The meeting's legal record is the Minutes approved by the City Council.

NOTICE
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, persons with a disability may request an agenda in appropriate alternative formats as required by Section 202 of the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990. Any person with a disability who requires a modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should direct such request to the City Clerk's office at (858) 720-2400 or by email at least 72 hours before the meeting.
As a courtesy to all meeting attendees, please set cellular phones and pagers to silent mode and engage in conversations outside the Council Chambers.
The Regular Meetings of the City Council are scheduled for the 2nd and 4th Wednesdays and are broadcast live on Cox Communications, Channel 19, and Time Warner, Channel 24. Council meetings are archived and available for viewing. The video taping of meetings are maintained as a permanent record and contain a detailed account of the proceedings.
A full City Council agenda packet with backup information is available at City Hall, at the Solana Beach branch of the San Diego County Library (157 Stevens Ave.), and online www.ci.solana-beach.ca.us at least 72 hours prior to the meeting. Agenda related writings or documents regarding an agenda item and that are received after the distribution of the agenda but at least 1 hour 30 minutes prior to the meeting will be available for public viewing at City Hall and posted online with the agenda.

Special Council Meeting
CITY OF SOLANA BEACH
Special Council Meeting
Solana Beach City Council, Redevelopment Agency, and Public Financing Authority
MINUTES
JOINT SPECIAL MEETING
Wednesday, May 11, 2011
08:00 P.M.
City Hall Council Chambers, 635 S. Highway 101, Solana Beach, California
The City Council acts as the City of Solana Beach Redevelopment Agency and the Public Financing Authority.
CALL TO ORDER AND ROLL CALL:
Present:
Heebner, Kellejian, Roberts, Nichols, and Campbell.
Absent:
None.
Also Present:
David Ott, City Manager
Johanna Canlas, City Attorney
Leticia Fallone, Deputy City Clerk
Angela Ivey, City Clerk
Dennis Coleman, Finance Director
Wende Protzman, Dir. Admin. Serv/Deputy City Mgr
Tina Christiansen, Community Dev. Dir.
Mo Sammak, City Engineer/Public Works Dir.
Mayor Heebner called the meeting to order at 8:05 p.m.
C.
STAFF REPORTS: (C.1.)
Submit speaker slips to the City Clerk
C.1.
Del Mar Fairgrounds Master Plan - Final Environmental Impact Report Certification. (File 0150-85)
Recommendation: That the City Council
1.
Discuss and provide direction.
David Ott, City Manager, introduced the item. He stated that the Fairground Board certified their Master Plan, that they committed to talk about some issues that could have an impact on the Solana Beach community, they removed the hotel from the Master Plan but not from the EIR, so the EIR was approved with the hotel option in it, which would have implications to the City. He said that they had never met with Solana Beach to talk about their proposal for the sports complex, which would be supplied with Solana Beach sewer services, which mandates their meeting with the City on the issue, and that they stated that it was San Diego providing the sewer services, but that they were incorrect. He continued stating that the City had 30 days to file a challenge, May 18th, and that it had retained Special Counsel who worked with the City on the original comments on the EIR and would work with them on reveiwing the potential challenge to their certified EIR. He said that he was directed by Council to discuss the issues with the City of Del Mar to see if they shared concerns, that initially the City Manager did not think they would want to join in some legal actions, that some subsequent meetings had them considering some possible legal challenge to the EIR, that Solana Beach drafted a cooperative agreement for the City to consider joining for potential legal action. He stated that Solana Beach had sent a letter in January requesting a 30 day delay for comments, and that they went to the minimum for public review, by law, that their General Manager stated that it was advice from their legal team, that in order to have any meaningful dialogue, with the quick movement, that the City felt it had no other choice but to challenge the EIR, and that they said they wanted to have a meaningful dialogue.
Mayor Heebner said that the door was shut in 30 days so the City would have to take action to protect the community’s interests and rights.
Councilmember Roberts said that when the Fairgrounds EIR came out that Solana Beach decided to spend taxpayer’s dollars to question assumptions and provide a very detailed response, that an EIR was supposed to show how impacts would be mitigateed for development, that the City had asked for a meaningful dialogue, and that the City had to take legal precautions in order to protect its rights.
MOTION: Moved by Roberts and seconded by Nichols to appoint Mayor Heebner to attend the next San Dieguito River Valley meeting on behalf of the current members.
Motion carried unanimously.
ADJOURN:
Mayor Heebner adjourned the meeting at 8:24 p.m.
________________________ Approved: November 16, 2011
Angela Ivey, City Clerk
